result.topic_en: Elasticity calculation: uniform hydrostatic compression and uniaxial tension of an isotropic elastic body with Lamé constants λ, μ, deriving the dilatation and the extension per unit tension (reciprocal Young's modulus).
result.transcription:
$u=ax\quad v=ay\quad w=az$
$N=(3\lambda+2\mu)a=-P$ \qquad $\theta=\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial w}{\partial z}=3a=-\frac{3\lambda}{3\lambda+2\mu}=\alpha$

$u=-ax\quad v=-ay\quad w=cz$

$F$, Zug auf die Flächeneinheit
$\theta=c-2a$
$N_1=N_2=(c-2a)\lambda-2a\mu=0$ \quad $N_3=(c-2a)\lambda+2c\mu=F$
$c\lambda-2a(\lambda+\mu)=0$ \qquad $c(\lambda+2\mu)-2a\lambda=F$
$\lambda c=2a(\lambda+\mu)$ \qquad $2a\frac{(\lambda+\mu)(\lambda+2\mu)-\lambda^2}{\lambda}=F=2a\frac{\mu(3\lambda+2\mu)}{\lambda}$
\qquad $\lambda^2+3\mu\lambda+2\mu^2$ \qquad $=c\frac{\mu(3\lambda+2\mu)}{\lambda+\mu}$

$\frac{c}{F}=\beta=\frac{\lambda+\mu}{\mu(3\lambda+2\mu)}$

methods.what: Normal stress under uniform dilatation (bulk response) for isotropic elastic body
Cubical dilatation as divergence of displacement
Uniaxial tension ansatz with lateral contraction
Hooke's law normal stresses in terms of Lamé constants with zero lateral stress
Relation between lateral contraction and axial extension (Poisson ratio relation)
Extension per unit tension (reciprocal Young's modulus) in Lamé constants
